questions.q: What are the two broad categories of embedding models used in production?
options: Supervised and unsupervised models
Text models and image models
Hosted API models and open-source/self-hosted models
Free models and paid models
questions.explain: Embedding models are either called over a hosted API (the provider runs the compute) or run on your own infrastructure as open-source/self-hosted models.

questions.q: What is a real advantage of a self-hosted embedding model like BGE or E5 over a hosted API model?
options: It always produces a higher MTEB score than every hosted model
It requires no infrastructure at all to run
It is always free to license commercially
Data never has to leave your own infrastructure, and it can be fine-tuned on your own domain
questions.explain: Self-hosted models trade upfront infrastructure effort for full data control and the ability to fine-tune on your own content — a real advantage for regulated or sensitive data.

questions.q: What is a real advantage of a hosted API embedding model over a self-hosted one?
options: No infrastructure to run, and typically strong general-purpose quality out of the box
It guarantees your data never leaves your own systems
It has no ongoing cost at any scale
It cannot be used for retrieval tasks
questions.explain: Hosted models remove the need to run your own inference infrastructure and generally provide strong quality with minimal setup, at the cost of ongoing per-token fees and a third-party dependency.

questions.q: What does MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) actually measure?
options: How much a given embedding model costs per API call
A standardized suite of tasks (retrieval, classification, clustering, similarity, etc.) across many languages and domains, averaged into a leaderboard score
Only how fast a model can generate vectors
Only how well a model performs on English Wikipedia
questions.explain: MTEB combines many different tasks and datasets into an overall leaderboard score, giving a broad (but generic) sense of a model's general-purpose embedding quality.

questions.q: Why shouldn't the top-ranked model on MTEB automatically be chosen for a specific project?
options: MTEB scores are updated too infrequently to be useful
MTEB's datasets are an average across general domains that may not resemble your specific documents, so a lower-ranked model can still outperform on your actual content
The top-ranked model is always the most expensive option
MTEB only evaluates image embeddings, not text
questions.explain: Because MTEB averages across many unrelated datasets, a model's overall rank doesn't guarantee it's the best fit for a narrow, specialized document set — testing against real data is what actually decides that.
